data.title: Build Process Lab HTMX flowsheet demo
Establish the flow-studio domain and SQLite repository
data.body:
## Goal
- Create the Go module, process-flow domain model, and SQLite-backed repository.
- Make one service own validation, persistence, and the caller-visible flow editing operations.

## Context
- The application is an educational single-user demo named Process Lab.
- Supported blocks are Source, Gain, First-order Lag, Sum, and Scope.
- A flow may branch and merge, but connections must remain acyclic.
- Block positions and parameters are persisted in SQLite.
- The service API exposes intent-revealing operations; HTTP handlers do not coordinate SQL transactions.
- Non-goals: authentication, collaboration, arbitrary user code, and production multi-tenancy.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A seeded example flowsheet is created on first run.
- Blocks and connections round-trip through SQLite.
- Invalid block parameters, duplicate connections, type-invalid connections, and cycles are rejected.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./internal/studio`

data.title: Compile and simulate user-created flows
data.body:
## Goal
- Compile a persisted flow graph into a continuous-time state-space model and simulate it with `github.com/jamestjsp/controlsys`.

## Context
- Pin `controlsys` to stable `v1.2.0` and include its required Gonum fork replacement.
- The source block produces the external step input; gain and sum blocks are algebraic; lag blocks contribute dynamic states; scopes define plotted outputs.
- Graph compilation owns topological ordering and matrix construction.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Branched and merged acyclic graphs simulate on a uniform time grid.
- Simulation returns time-series data plus peak, final value, and settling indicators.
- Missing sources/scopes, cyclic graphs, and invalid lag constants return actionable errors.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./internal/studio -run 'TestSimulate|TestCompile'`

data.title: Build the HTMX process-flow workbench
data.body:
## Goal
- Deliver the server-rendered workbench and interactive editing endpoints.

## Context
- Use Go `html/template` and HTMX 2.0.10.
- HTMX owns server interactions and HTML fragment replacement.
- A small local JavaScript layer owns pointer dragging, connect-mode gestures, keyboard shortcuts, and SVG edge redraws because those are browser-local interactions.
- Return out-of-band fragments when one mutation affects the canvas, inspector, and status panels.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Users can add, select, configure, drag, connect, and delete blocks without full-page reloads.
- Users can run a simulation and receive an SVG trend plot plus metrics.
- The interface includes a palette, flowsheet canvas, properties inspector, status bar, and responsive small-screen behavior.
- Errors render inline and preserve the current workbench.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./internal/web`
- `go test ./...`

data.title: Document and verify the runnable demo
data.body:
## Goal
- Make the demo straightforward to run, inspect, and extend.

## Context
- Document architecture, HTMX interaction examples, SQLite location, supported block semantics, and controlsys integration.
- Keep all runtime assets embedded in the Go binary except the documented HTMX CDN script.

## Acceptance Criteria
- README includes prerequisites, run command, test command, interaction walkthrough, and architecture map.
- A clean build starts with a usable seeded flowsheet.
- Formatting, vet, tests, and production build pass.
- Browser validation covers add, drag, connect, edit, simulate, delete, refresh persistence, and responsive layout.

## Validation Gates
- `gofmt -w .`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test -race ./...`
- `go build ./cmd/processlab`

data.title: Simulink-grade workbench ergonomics
Widen the flowsheet coordinate world
data.body:
## Goal
- Raise the sheet from a 1040x500 box to a 6000x4000 world so pan and zoom have somewhere to go.

## Context
- `internal/studio/model.go:168` `clampPosition` currently pins X to 20..1040 and Y to 20..500. That is barely one screen, which makes panning pointless.
- `internal/studio/studio.go:302` `openPosition` searches a hardcoded fallback lattice (`y` in 90/220/350/470, `x` in 30..930) when the desired spot is taken. It must cover the new world and keep new blocks near the top-left origin so they land where the user is looking.
- `internal/web/view.go:154` `edgePath` hardcodes the block size (`+172` width, `+42` half-height). Extract those to named constants shared with the collision check in `openPosition` (which uses 172 and 84) so one edit changes both.
- Existing rows in `processlab.db` hold small coordinates; widening the clamp is backward compatible and needs no migration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `clampPosition` accepts 0..6000 in X and 0..4000 in Y, still rejecting negative values by clamping to the grid origin (0, 0).
- Coordinates are snapped to the 20px sheet grid by the domain, so a value of 37 stores as 40. This makes the grid authoritative on the server, not just a client affordance.
- `openPosition` walks a lattice derived from the block footprint and the new world size, tries positions in reading order from the origin, and only fails when the world is genuinely full.
- Block width, height, and grid pitch are exported named constants (for example `BlockWidth`, `BlockHeight`, `GridPitch`, `SheetWidth`, `SheetHeight`) in the studio package. `internal/web/view.go` consumes them instead of its own literals.
- Existing tests still pass; add cases for snapping, for the new bounds, and for placing a block when the origin lattice cell is occupied.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./...`
- `go vet ./...`

data.title: Rebuild the shell as a full-viewport workspace
data.body:
## Goal
- Replace the page-scrolling stacked layout with a 100vh application shell so the canvas is the only region that grows.

## Context
- `internal/web/templates/workbench.html` renders `.workbench` > `.topbar` + `.studio-grid` (palette / main-stage / inspector) + `.statusbar`. `.main-stage` scrolls the canvas card and results card together, so the canvas can never fill the height.
- `internal/web/static/app.css:40` `.workbench` uses `grid-template-rows: 72px auto 1fr 32px`; `.flow-canvas:454` is a fixed `height: 590px`.
- Target shell from the approved wireframe:
  - `.workbench` is `height: 100dvh; display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto auto 1fr auto`, `overflow: hidden`, and the document body never scrolls.
  - `.studio-grid` is `grid-template-columns: var(--rail-left) minmax(0, 1fr) var(--rail-right)` with `min-height: 0` so the middle column can shrink.
  - The middle column stacks canvas (`1fr`) over a resize handle over the simulation dock (`var(--dock-height)`).
- Rails collapse to a 46px icon strip rather than vanishing: the palette keeps its glyph buttons (still clickable to add a block) and the inspector keeps a vertical label. Full hide is available too, giving three states is not worth it, so collapse means icon strip.
- Collapse toggles live on the rail edge and in the topbar. State keys: `processlab:rail-left`, `processlab:rail-right`, `processlab:dock-height`, read on load in `app.js` and written on change. Apply state as `data-rail-left="collapsed"` / `data-dock="collapsed"` attributes on `#workbench` so CSS drives all the sizing.
- Because HTMX swaps `#workbench` wholesale on nearly every action, the shell state must be re-applied after `htmx:afterSwap`. Read it from localStorage in one `applyShellState()` and call it on load and after every swap. Alternatively render the attributes server-side, do not: this is per-user view state and does not belong in the flow record.

## Acceptance Criteria
- At any viewport height the page itself does not scroll; only the palette list, inspector body, and dock body scroll internally.
- Collapsing both rails leaves the canvas occupying the full width between them minus the two 46px strips.
- The dock can be dragged between a collapsed header-only state and 70vh, and the canvas reflows live during the drag.
- Collapsed and expanded states survive a page reload and every HTMX swap.
- Keyboard: the collapse toggles are real `<button>` elements with `aria-expanded` and visible focus rings.
- The existing responsive breakpoints still produce a usable layout at 860px and 620px wide; the rails auto-collapse below 1100px.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./...`
- `go run ./cmd/processlab` then confirm in a browser at 1440x900 and 1280x720: no page scrollbar, rails collapse, dock resizes, state persists across reload.

data.title: Add a pan and zoom viewport to the canvas
data.body:
## Goal
- Give the sheet a real viewport: pan by dragging, zoom about the cursor, fit to contents, and a live zoom readout.

## Context
- Today `.flow-canvas` is a fixed 590px `overflow: auto` box, `#draft-edge` and drag math read `offsetLeft`/`scrollLeft` directly (`app.js:78`, `app.js:104`), and the toolbar zoom readout at `workbench.html:77` is a hardcoded `100%` string.
- Introduce a transformed sheet layer inside the viewport:
  - `.flow-canvas` becomes `overflow: hidden; position: relative` and fills its grid cell.
  - A new `#sheet` child holds the SVG connection layer and all `.block-card` elements, with `transform: translate(Xpx, Ypx) scale(Z); transform-origin: 0 0; will-change: transform`.
  - Blocks keep their existing absolute sheet coordinates, so no template coordinate math changes.
  - The SVG connection layer gets `width`/`height` equal to the world size from the studio constants and drops `preserveAspectRatio="none"` and the 1240x590 viewBox, which currently distorts edges.
- The grid stays on the viewport element, not the sheet, drawn with `background-size: calc(pitch * Z)` and `background-position` tracking pan. This gives an infinite grid without a giant element. Subdivide the pattern at zoom thresholds so the fine grid disappears below 60% zoom and a coarse 100px lattice appears above 150%.
- Central helper `screenToSheet(clientX, clientY)` returning sheet coordinates. Every interaction (drag, draft wire, later the marquee) must go through it instead of reading `offsetLeft`/`scrollLeft`.
- Input bindings, chosen to match Figma and Simulink habits so they need no explanation:
  - `ctrl`/`cmd` + wheel and trackpad pinch zoom about the pointer.
  - Plain wheel pans (`deltaX`/`deltaY`), matching every modern canvas tool.
  - Middle-drag and space+drag pan; the cursor becomes `grab`/`grabbing`.
  - `cmd/ctrl` + `=` / `-` zoom in steps, `cmd/ctrl` + `0` resets to 100%, `shift` + `1` fits contents.
- Zoom range 25% to 400%. Fit computes the bounding box of all blocks, pads it by one block width, and picks the scale that shows everything without exceeding 100%.
- Viewport state persists to `processlab:viewport:<flowID>` in localStorage and is re-applied after each HTMX swap alongside the shell state.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Zooming with the pointer over a specific block keeps that block under the pointer.
- The zoom readout in the toolbar shows the real integer percentage and updates live.
- Panning never reveals a hard scroll edge inside the visible viewport; the sheet bounds only constrain where blocks may be dropped, not where the user may look.
- Dragging a block at 50% and at 300% zoom tracks the pointer exactly, with no drift or acceleration.
- The draft wire drawn while connecting follows the pointer correctly at every zoom level.
- Connection paths stay hairline-crisp at all zooms (`vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke` retained).
- Viewport survives reload and HTMX swaps; a swap never snaps the view back to the origin.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` suppresses the smooth-zoom easing.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./...`
- Browser check: zoom to 25% and 400%, pan to the far corner of the world, add a block, drag it, wire it, and confirm all four behave correctly at non-100% zoom.

data.title: Snap block drags to the sheet grid
data.body:
## Goal
- Make block placement land on the grid with live alignment feedback, so diagrams look drafted rather than hand-placed.

## Context
- Depends on the viewport task for `screenToSheet`, and on the domain task for `GridPitch` and server-side snapping.
- `app.js:104` `moveDrag` writes raw pixel offsets and clamps against `scrollWidth`. Replace with sheet-space math plus snapping.
- Snap rounds the block's top-left to the nearest `GridPitch` (20px). Holding `alt` bypasses snapping for fine placement, which is the standard escape hatch.
- Add alignment guides: while dragging, if the moving block's centre or either edge is within 4px of another block's, draw a full-height or full-width guide line on the sheet and snap to that alignment. Cap the comparison to blocks currently in view to keep it cheap.
- The drag currently commits with a `PATCH /blocks/{id}/position` on pointerup and leaves the DOM position as the client set it. Keep that, but send the snapped value so client and server agree.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A dragged block visibly settles onto grid intersections during the drag, not just on release.
- Alt-dragging places a block at an arbitrary coordinate; releasing alt re-engages snapping.
- Alignment guides appear only while dragging, disappear on release, and are drawn in the sheet layer so they scale with zoom.
- The position persisted to SQLite equals the position rendered on screen after a reload.
- Snapping is correct at 25% and 400% zoom (snap in sheet space, never in screen space).

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./...`
- Browser check: drag a block, reload, confirm it has not moved. Repeat at 200% zoom.

data.title: Select multiple blocks with a marquee
data.body:
## Goal
- Support rubber-band and shift-click selection, and move the whole selection as one, which is the single biggest gap against Simulink.

## Context
- Depends on the viewport and snap tasks.
- Selection model: a client-side `Set` of block IDs in `app.js` is the source of truth for multi-selection. The server keeps its existing single `selected` query parameter for the inspector, so the HTMX contract is unchanged.
  - Selection of exactly one block does the normal server round-trip and shows the parameter inspector.
  - Selection of two or more skips the round-trip and renders a client-side summary card into a `#selection-panel` slot that `workbench.html` always emits (empty when unused). Rationale: a server trip per marquee drag would be wasteful and would fight the inspector's form state.
- Marquee: pointerdown on empty sheet starts a rubber band drawn in the viewport layer in screen space; on release, convert to sheet space and intersect against block rectangles using `BlockWidth`/`BlockHeight`. Shift extends the selection, plain drag replaces it.
- Shift-click or cmd-click on a block toggles it in the selection.
- Dragging any selected block moves every selected block by the same delta, with snapping applied to the primary block and the same delta applied to the rest so relative spacing is preserved exactly.
- New batch endpoint, because sending N parallel PATCH requests would be both slow and non-atomic:
  - `PATCH /flows/{flowID}/blocks/positions` accepting repeated `id`, `x`, `y` form values.
  - Domain operation `MoveBlocks(ctx, flowID int64, moves []BlockMove) error` applying all moves in one transaction and rejecting the request if any block does not belong to the flow.
  - Return `204 No Content` like the existing single move.
- Selection must be re-applied to the DOM after every `htmx:afterSwap`, since the swap replaces all block elements. Drop IDs that no longer exist.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Dragging on empty canvas draws a marquee and selects every block it touches; dragging on a block moves instead of marquee-selecting.
- Shift-drag adds to the existing selection rather than replacing it.
- Moving a 3-block selection preserves the relative offsets between them and persists all three positions in one request.
- The selection summary card reports the count and offers Delete and Fit-to-selection actions.
- Selecting a single block still opens the full parameter inspector exactly as before.
- A batch move that names a block from another flow is rejected with 400 and moves nothing.
- Selection survives an unrelated HTMX swap, such as running a simulation.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./...` including a new `internal/web/server_test.go` case for the batch endpoint covering the happy path, mismatched array lengths, and a foreign block ID.
- Browser check: marquee-select three blocks, drag them, reload, confirm the arrangement is preserved.

data.title: Wire signals by dragging between ports
data.body:
## Goal
- Let a user press an output port and drag to an input port to make a connection, the way every schematic editor works.

## Context
- Depends on the viewport task.
- Today `app.js:154` starts a connection on pointerdown over an output port and completes it on a separate pointerdown over an input port. That click-then-click flow stays as the keyboard and accessibility path, but drag becomes the primary gesture.
- Implement as: pointerdown on an output port captures the pointer and enters a wiring state; pointermove draws the draft edge through `screenToSheet`; pointerup over a valid input port commits, pointerup anywhere else cancels with a status message. If the pointer never moved more than a few pixels, fall back to the existing sticky click-then-click mode so both gestures coexist.
- Add drop-target feedback: while wiring, valid input ports enlarge and pulse (the `.is-connecting` styling already exists), and the port directly under the pointer gets a distinct `hover-target` state. Invalid targets (the source block itself, an already-connected input on a single-input block) render with a `not-allowed` cursor and do not commit.
- The server already rejects invalid connections in `studio.Connect`; the client-side feedback is an affordance, not the validation.
- Ports are small targets at low zoom. Give each port an invisible hit area that stays a constant screen size by counter-scaling the padding with zoom, so wiring is still practical at 40%.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Press-drag-release from an output port to an input port creates the connection in one gesture.
- Releasing over empty canvas cancels cleanly and leaves no draft edge.
- Click-then-click wiring still works, and Escape still cancels it.
- The draft edge tracks the pointer accurately at 25% and 400% zoom.
- Ports remain clickable at 40% zoom without pixel-hunting.
- Attempting a self-connection gives immediate visual rejection rather than a server round-trip and an error banner.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./...`
- Browser check: wire a Step to a Gain by dragging at 100%, then at 40%, then at 300%.

data.title: Add workbench keyboard shortcuts
data.body:
## Goal
- Cover the keyboard vocabulary an engineer expects, so common edits never require the mouse.

## Context
- Depends on the marquee selection task for the selection model.
- `app.js:179` currently handles only Escape and cmd+Enter.
- Bindings to add:
  - `Delete` / `Backspace` removes the current selection, after a confirmation only when more than one block is selected.
  - Arrow keys nudge the selection by one grid pitch; `shift` + arrows nudge by five.
  - `cmd/ctrl` + `a` selects every block; `Escape` clears the selection as well as cancelling a wire.
  - `cmd/ctrl` + `d` duplicates the selection, offset by one grid step.
  - `cmd/ctrl` + `=` / `-` / `0` and `shift` + `1` for zoom, wired to the viewport task's helpers.
- Every binding must no-op while focus is inside an `input` or a `textarea`, otherwise typing a parameter value will delete blocks. This is the most likely defect in this task, so guard it first.
- New endpoints required:
  - `POST /flows/{flowID}/blocks/duplicate` taking repeated `id` values, copying kind, parameters, and name (suffixed to stay unique) at an offset position.
  - `DELETE /flows/{flowID}/blocks` taking repeated `id` values, with a `DeleteBlocks` domain operation that removes the blocks and their connections in one transaction.
- Add a discoverable shortcut sheet: a `?` key opens a modal listing every binding, and the status bar links to it. Undocumented shortcuts may as well not exist.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Typing in any inspector field never triggers a shortcut, including the name field where `d` and `a` are ordinary characters.
- Deleting a multi-block selection removes every block and every connection touching them, in one request.
- Duplicating two connected blocks produces two new blocks with the parameters copied; connections between the originals are not copied (state this in the shortcut sheet so it is not a surprise).
- Arrow-key nudges persist through the batch move endpoint and land on grid.
- The shortcut sheet is reachable by keyboard, dismissible with Escape, and returns focus to the canvas.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./...` including handler tests for batch delete and duplicate.
- Browser check: select two blocks, press an arrow key, reload, confirm both moved one pitch. Then focus the name field and press Delete, confirming nothing is deleted.

data.title: Add canvas context menus
data.body:
## Goal
- Put the frequent block actions one right-click away instead of a trip to the inspector rail.

## Context
- Depends on the keyboard task, which introduces the duplicate and batch-delete endpoints this reuses.
- Suppress the native menu only over the sheet, never over the rails or the dock, so the browser's own menu stays available where it is useful.
- Two menus:
  - On a block: Rename (focuses the inspector name field), Duplicate, Delete, Disconnect all wires, Fit to this block.
  - On empty canvas: Paste position-aware new block via a compact block picker, Select all, Fit to contents, Reset zoom.
- Right-clicking an unselected block selects it first; right-clicking inside an existing multi-selection keeps that selection and shows the plural actions.
- Menu is a single `#context-menu` element positioned in viewport coordinates, closed on Escape, on outside pointerdown, on scroll, and on any HTMX swap. Arrow keys and Enter navigate it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The menu never renders off-screen; near a viewport edge it flips to stay fully visible.
- Menu actions operate on the whole selection when more than one block is selected, and the labels reflect the count.
- Escape and an outside click both dismiss without performing an action.
- The menu is keyboard-navigable and each item has an accessible name.
- Right-clicking the palette or the dock shows the normal browser menu.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./...`
- Browser check: right-click a block near the bottom-right corner and confirm the menu flips and stays visible.

data.title: Establish the workbench design system
data.body:
## Goal
- Give the workbench the visual language of an instrument, and fix a type scale that is currently unreadable.

## Context
- Depends on the shell task, which creates the surfaces this styles.
- Two concrete problems in `internal/web/static/app.css` today:
  1. Type is 7px to 9px across the entire interface (`.palette-item small` is 9px, `.block-kind` is 7px, `.statusbar` is 8px, `.activity-section small` is 7px). This is below any usable floor and is the single largest readability defect in the app.
  2. The palette is cream `#f4f2ec` with a Georgia serif display and a terracotta accent, which is the most common generated-design default there is. It also reads as a document rather than a tool.
- Direction: annunciator panel. The chrome is a machined dark housing; the sheet is cool drafting vellum; numbers are the hero and are always monospace. Derive every value from these tokens:
  - `--sheet: #eef1ef` cool vellum canvas, replacing the yellow cream.
  - `--housing: #16201e` and `--housing-raised: #1f2c29` for rails, toolbars, status bar.
  - `--signal: #e2673a` reserved exclusively for signal wires and output ports, so orange always means "carries a signal".
  - `--probe: #35b39c` for interactive and valid-target affordances, brightened from the current `#2d8b80` which is too dim against dark chrome.
  - `--caution: #d9a441` for sum blocks and warnings.
  - `--ink: #101a18` on light surfaces, `--ink-inverse: #e8efec` on the housing.
- Typography: drop the Georgia display face from the chrome. Instruments do not set their labels in a book serif. Use the grotesque for all labels and promote `ui-monospace` with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` to a first-class role for every numeric readout: coordinates, zoom, gains, metrics, timestamps, block parameter summaries. Type scale floor of 11px, stepping 11 / 12 / 13 / 15 / 19 / 24.
- Signature element, the readout rail: rebuild the status bar as a live monospace instrument strip showing cursor position in sheet coordinates, zoom, grid pitch, selection count, block and signal counts, and solver state. Pair it with the zoom-responsive grid from the viewport task so the sheet visibly behaves like a CAD drawing. This is where the boldness is spent; everything else stays quiet.
- Keep the existing block accent colours by category, they already encode real information.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No user-facing text is set below 11px anywhere in `app.css`.
- Every numeric readout uses the mono face with tabular figures, so digits do not jitter as values change.
- Body text on every surface meets WCAG AA contrast; verify the muted greys against both the vellum sheet and the dark housing, which is where the current palette fails.
- The status bar reports live cursor sheet coordinates and updates as the pointer moves over the canvas.
- Focus is visible on every interactive element against both light and dark surfaces.
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` disables the transitions added here.
- Colour is never the only signal: selected blocks carry an outline as well as a hue change.

## Validation Gates
- `grep -nE 'font-size:\s*([0-9]|10)px' internal/web/static/app.css` returns nothing.
- `go test ./...`
- Browser check at 1440x900: confirm the readout rail tracks the cursor and that the interface reads clearly at arm's length.

data.title: Verify and document the workbench
data.body:
## Goal
- Prove the whole interaction set works together and leave the demo documented.

## Context
- Depends on every other task in this container.
- `README.md` documents the current click-to-wire flow and must be updated to the new gestures.
- `docs/simulink-block-expansion.md` is the precedent for a feature write-up; add a sibling `docs/workbench-ergonomics.md`.
- `internal/web/server_test.go` covers the existing handlers; extend it rather than starting a new file.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Handler tests cover the batch move, batch delete, and duplicate endpoints, including rejection of IDs from another flow.
- Domain tests cover position snapping, the widened bounds, and `openPosition` when the origin lattice is occupied.
- `README.md` describes the shell, the rails, the dock, and the full gesture and keyboard vocabulary.
- `docs/workbench-ergonomics.md` records the interaction model, the chosen key bindings and why, the viewport and selection state model, and the localStorage keys, so the next change does not have to rediscover them.
- A manual verification pass at 1440x900 and 1280x720 exercises: collapse both rails, resize the dock, pan and zoom, snap-drag, marquee-move three blocks, drag-wire, delete via keyboard, and the context menu. Record the result in the doc.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` returns nothing.

## Goal
- Bring the Process Lab flowsheet workbench up to the interaction standard of a desktop block-diagram editor. Today the sheet is a fixed 590px box on a scrolling page, positions are clamped to 1040x500, there is no pan, no zoom, no snapping, no multi-select, and the side rails cannot be collapsed.

## Scope
- Full-viewport application shell with collapsible palette and inspector rails and a resizable simulation dock.
- Pan, zoom, fit-to-contents, and a grid that responds to zoom.
- Grid snapping enforced by the domain, with alignment guides on the client.
- Marquee and shift-click multi-selection with a batched move.
- Drag-to-wire between ports, keeping click-then-click for keyboard users.
- Keyboard vocabulary: delete, nudge, select-all, duplicate, zoom, plus a discoverable shortcut sheet.
- Right-click context menus on blocks and on empty canvas.
- A design pass that fixes an unusable 7-9px type scale and moves the chrome away from a generic look.

## Non-goals
- Undo/redo. It needs a command history in the domain and is a container of its own.
- Server-persisted viewport or selection state. Both are per-user view state.
- Subsystems, block rotation, or multi-port blocks.
- Collaborative or multi-user editing.
- Touch and pen input beyond what pointer events give for free.

## Decisions
- **Shell**: full-viewport grid, no page scroll, canvas is the sole growing region, results become a bottom dock. Chosen over floating overlay panels because overlays obscure the diagram, which is the thing the user is working on.
- **Collapse means icon strip, not hide.** A collapsed palette keeps its glyph buttons so blocks can still be added; a collapsed inspector keeps a vertical label. Three states would be worth less than the simplicity of two.
- **Sheet world is a large fixed 6000x4000 with 25-400% zoom**, not unbounded. Keeps `clampPosition` a real validation guard and makes fit-to-contents well defined, while being effectively unlimited for any diagram this tool will hold.
- **The grid is authoritative on the server.** `clampPosition` snaps to the 20px pitch, so a hand-edited or replayed request cannot produce off-grid blocks.
- **Viewport, rail, dock, and selection state live in localStorage**, keyed by flow where relevant, and are re-applied after every HTMX swap. They are not part of the flow record.
- **Multi-selection is client-side.** The server keeps its single `selected` parameter for the inspector, so the existing HTMX contract is untouched. Two or more selected blocks render a client-side summary card instead of a server round-trip.
- **Drag-to-wire is primary, click-then-click is retained**, not replaced, because the sticky mode is the keyboard-accessible path.
- **Batched endpoints over N requests**: move, delete, and duplicate each take repeated IDs and run in one transaction. Per-block requests would be slow and non-atomic.

## Constraints
- HTMX swaps `#workbench` wholesale on nearly every action. Any client-held state must survive `htmx:afterSwap`; this is the recurring failure mode across the whole container and every task that holds state must re-apply it.
- No build step and no new runtime dependency. The CSP in `internal/web/server.go:287` allows scripts only from self and the HTMX CDN.
- Templates are Go `html/template` in `internal/web/templates`; static assets are embedded via `go:embed`.

## Risks
- Coordinate bugs at non-100% zoom are the likeliest defect class. Every interaction must convert through one shared `screenToSheet` helper rather than reading `offsetLeft`/`scrollLeft`.
- Keyboard shortcuts firing while a parameter field has focus would destroy user work. Guard before implementing the bindings.

data.text:
Widened the sheet to a 6000x4000 world with a 20px authoritative grid.

Exported GridPitch, BlockWidth, BlockHeight, SheetWidth, SheetHeight from the studio package; clampPosition now snaps to the grid and keeps the whole block inside the sheet. openPosition walks a lattice derived from the block footprint (240x120 step from a 60,80 origin) instead of a hardcoded 24-cell list. view.go consumes the constants instead of its own 172/42 literals.

Found and fixed: the seeded demo flowsheet was laid out off-grid and bypassed clampPosition entirely on insert. Seeds now run through clampPosition and sit on the lattice.

Verified with gofmt -l (clean), go vet, go test ./... — all pass, including three new tests covering snapping, the widened bounds, and non-overlap when the lattice fills.

Rebuilt the workbench as a 100dvh application shell. workbench.html: added topbar shell toggles, rail heads with collapse buttons, a vertical inspector label, a scrolling .inspector-body, a .dock-resizer separator and a .dock-body wrapper around the results. app.css: .workbench is height:100dvh grid (auto auto 1fr auto, explicit grid-row per child) with shell custom properties; .studio-grid uses var(--rail-left) minmax(0,1fr) var(--rail-right); .main-stage stacks canvas 1fr / resizer / var(--dock-height); .flow-canvas is now a relative overflow:hidden box filling its cell (no pan/zoom added); collapse rules gated behind min-width:861px so the stacked breakpoints are untouched. app.js: added a separate shell-state section with one applyShellState() reading processlab:rail-left / rail-right / dock-height from localStorage, writing data-rail-left/right and data-dock plus an inline --dock-height on #workbench, called on load, DOMContentLoaded, htmx:afterSwap, htmx:afterSettle, resize and matchMedia change. Existing connection/drag logic untouched. Verified with go build/vet/test/gofmt plus a headless Chrome CDP run: no page scroll at 1440x900, 1280x720 or 1099x800; rails collapse to exactly 46px each (canvas 1322px of 1440); state survives reload and an HTMX block-add swap; dock drags live down to the 58px header-only state and up to a 630px 70vh clamp, persists across reload; rails auto-collapse strictly below 1100px with a user toggle overriding; toggles are buttons with aria-expanded and 2px focus-visible rings; 860px and 620px layouts render with no horizontal overflow.

Added a pan/zoom viewport. #sheet carries translate+scale inside a clipped #flow-canvas; the grid is painted on the viewport with background-size/position tracking zoom and pan, so it stays infinite without a 6000x4000 tiled element, and the fine lattice drops out below 60%.

All pointer math now routes through one screenToSheet helper. Go constants reach the client via data attributes on #flow-canvas (new sheetGeometry in view.go), so the client cannot drift from the domain.

Bindings: ctrl/cmd+wheel and pinch zoom about the cursor, plain wheel pans, space-drag and middle-drag pan, cmd +/-/0, shift+1 fits. Range 25-400%. State persists per flow in localStorage.

Two real bugs found and fixed during verification:
1. Restoring the viewport on htmx:afterSwap alone does not work: at that point querySelector still returns the node htmx is about to discard, so the style was written to a doomed element and the view snapped to origin on every edit. Restoring on afterSettle as well is what sticks.
2. The old fixed 1240x590 SVG viewBox with preserveAspectRatio=none was distorting every edge; removed in favour of a world-sized SVG.

Verified with a CDP harness driving real gestures: 18/18 checks, including zoom-anchor drift of 2.8e-14 sheet units, drag tracking exact at 33% and 204% zoom, draft-wire endpoint error 0.00px, and viewport surviving both reload and a real HTMX swap.

data.body:
## Goal
- Let a user press an output port and drag to an input port to make a connection, the way every schematic editor works.

## Context
- Depends on the viewport task, which is done. Use its `screenToSheet(clientX, clientY)` helper for all pointer maths; never read `offsetLeft`/`scrollLeft` directly.
- Today `app.js` starts a connection on pointerdown over an output port and completes it on a separate pointerdown over an input port. That click-then-click flow stays as the keyboard and accessibility path, but drag becomes the primary gesture.
- Implement as: pointerdown on an output port captures the pointer and enters a wiring state; pointermove draws the draft edge through `screenToSheet`; pointerup over a valid input port commits, pointerup anywhere else cancels with a status message. If the pointer never moved more than a few pixels, fall back to the existing sticky click-then-click mode so both gestures coexist.
- Add drop-target feedback: while wiring, valid input ports enlarge and pulse (the `.is-connecting` styling already exists), and the port directly under the pointer gets a distinct `hover-target` state. Invalid targets (the source block itself, an already-connected input on a single-input block) render with a `not-allowed` cursor and do not commit.
- The server already rejects invalid connections in `studio.Connect`; the client-side feedback is an affordance, not the validation.
- Ports are small targets at low zoom. Give each port an invisible hit area that stays a constant screen size by counter-scaling the padding with zoom, so wiring is still practical at 40%.

## Known defect this task must fix
- **Ports are occluded by neighbouring blocks.** `.block-card` sets `position: absolute; z-index: 5`, which makes each card its own stacking context. A port's `z-index: 10` is therefore scoped inside its own card, so any card later in DOM order paints over an earlier card's ports. Confirmed with `document.elementFromPoint` returning `.block-body` of a neighbouring card at a port's exact centre, which makes that port unclickable. Fix it (for example by raising the card's z-index on hover and while wiring, and/or giving ports their own layer), and assert with `elementFromPoint` that every port is the topmost element at its own centre in a crowded flowsheet.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Press-drag-release from an output port to an input port creates the connection in one gesture.
- Releasing over empty canvas cancels cleanly and leaves no draft edge.
- Click-then-click wiring still works, and Escape still cancels it.
- The draft edge tracks the pointer accurately at 25% and 400% zoom.
- Ports remain clickable at 40% zoom without pixel-hunting.
- Every output and input port is hit-testable via `elementFromPoint` even when blocks are adjacent or overlapping.
- Attempting a self-connection gives immediate visual rejection rather than a server round-trip and an error banner.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./...`
- Rebuild before any browser check: templates and static assets are `go:embed`-ed, so editing `app.js` alone changes nothing the server serves.
- Browser check: wire a Step to a Gain by dragging at 100%, then at 40%, then at 300%.

## Goal
- Make block placement land on the grid with live alignment feedback, so diagrams look drafted rather than hand-placed.

## Context
- Depends on the viewport task for `screenToSheet`, and on the domain task for `GridPitch` and server-side snapping. Both are done.
- Snapping happens in sheet space, never screen space, or the step size would change with zoom.
- Alignment guides: while dragging, if the moving block's centre or either edge is within 5px of another block's, snap to that alignment and draw a hairline guide. Guides are counter-scaled by zoom so they stay hairlines. The comparison is capped to nearby blocks.
- Guides are created as inline-styled elements inside `#sheet` rather than styled from `app.css`, because a concurrent task owns that stylesheet.

## Decision: Alt suspends alignment only, never the grid
- The task originally promised Alt-drag for arbitrary off-grid placement. That conflicts with the container decision that the server's grid is authoritative: `clampPosition` snaps every stored position, so an off-grid client placement would be silently rewritten and the block would jump on the next reload, breaking the "rendered position equals persisted position" criterion.
- Resolved in favour of the authoritative grid, which is the more valuable invariant and the reason the domain task moved snapping server-side. Alt now suspends only the neighbour-alignment magnetism, which is the case where users actually want to escape a snap (placing a block deliberately just off a neighbour's edge). Grid snapping is unconditional, so client and server never disagree.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A dragged block visibly settles onto grid intersections during the drag, not just on release.
- Holding Alt suspends alignment magnetism; the block still lands on the grid.
- Alignment guides appear only while dragging, disappear on release, and stay hairlines at every zoom.
- The position persisted to SQLite equals the position rendered on screen after a reload.
- Snapping is correct at 25% and 400% zoom.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./...`
- Rebuild before any browser check: templates and static assets are `go:embed`-ed, so editing `app.js` alone changes nothing the server serves.
- Browser check: drag a block, reload, confirm it has not moved. Repeat at 200% zoom.

data.text:
Grid snapping with neighbour-alignment guides.

Snapping happens in sheet space so the step is zoom-independent. Alignment magnetism (edges and centres, 5px threshold) overrides plain grid snapping and draws hairline guides counter-scaled by zoom; comparison is capped to nearby blocks.

Resolved a conflict in the plan: the task promised Alt-drag for arbitrary off-grid placement, but the container decided the server grid is authoritative. Those cannot both hold - clampPosition would rewrite the position and the block would jump on reload. Kept the authoritative grid; Alt now suspends only alignment magnetism. Recorded in the task body.

Found and fixed: alignment could itself produce off-grid positions, because a block is 172x84 while the grid is 20, so centre and far-edge alignments land between intersections. Caught by a check comparing rendered against reloaded position (rendered 404 vs stored 400). Alignment candidates are now filtered to those that are themselves on-grid.

Verified with CDP: 13/13 checks, including grid landing at 25% and 199% zoom, rendered-equals-persisted after reload at both, guides appearing and clearing, and Alt suppressing alignment while still landing on-grid.

Marquee and shift-click multi-selection with batched move and delete.

Selection is a client-side Set; the server keeps its single 'selected' parameter for the inspector, so the HTMX contract is unchanged and a marquee costs no round trips. The set is re-applied after every swap and ids that no longer exist are dropped; with nothing selected it defers to the server-rendered selection so a swap never drops the inspector highlight.

Marquee bands in sheet space with live highlighting as it sweeps, shift extends. Dragging any selected block moves the whole selection by one delta, so relative spacing is preserved exactly.

Go: added MoveBlocks and DeleteBlocks (both single-transaction, both rejecting ids outside the flow), PATCH /flows/{id}/blocks/positions and DELETE /flows/{id}/blocks.

Scope change: batch delete was planned for the keyboard task, but the selection bar needs it, so the endpoint and domain operation landed here. QPCX4X now only binds the key to it.

Instead of a server-rendered #selection-panel slot, the multi-selection summary is a client-rendered action bar floating over the canvas - contextual to the work rather than parked in the inspector rail, and it avoided editing a template another agent held.

Verified: go test (including handler tests for the batch endpoint covering the happy path, mismatched arrays and a foreign block id) plus 15/15 CDP checks covering marquee, shift-extend, uniform group delta, on-grid landing, persistence, survival of a simulation-run swap, single-click inspector, and batch delete.

Keyboard vocabulary plus a discoverable shortcut sheet.

Bindings: Delete/Backspace deletes the selection, arrows nudge one grid step (shift = five), Cmd/Ctrl+A selects all, Cmd/Ctrl+D duplicates, Escape clears the selection as well as cancelling a wire, and the zoom keys from the viewport task. '?' opens a modal sheet documenting all 20 bindings.

The input-focus guard runs before every binding, so typing a block name cannot delete or duplicate anything. Also found and fixed a collision with the dock resizer, which binds arrow keys while focused: the resizer keeps them when it has focus.

Go: added DuplicateBlocks and POST /flows/{id}/blocks/duplicate. Copies kind, parameters and a distinct '<name> copy' name at an offset position; wires between originals are deliberately not copied, and the shortcut sheet says so. Batch delete landed with TEG3VU, so this task only bound the key.

Also wired the readout rail values the design agent's markup exposes: live cursor sheet coordinates, zoom, grid pitch and selection count.

Verified: go test including handler tests for duplicate (happy path, foreign id duplicates nothing, wires not invented) and batch delete cascading, plus 16/16 CDP checks - most importantly that Backspace, Delete, Cmd+D and Cmd+A all no-op while the inspector name field has focus.

Outstanding: the status bar still needs a visible link to the shortcut sheet; the design agent holds that markup, so it is being added once it lands.

Context menus on blocks and on empty canvas.

Block menu: Rename (selects the block and focuses the inspector name field once the swap settles), Duplicate, Disconnect all wires, Fit, Delete. Labels become plural and act on the whole selection when more than one block is selected. Right-clicking outside the current selection re-targets it; inside it, the selection is kept.

Canvas menu: a block picker that places the block exactly where you right-clicked (snapped to grid), plus Select all, Fit to contents and Reset zoom. The picker reads the catalogue off the palette rather than duplicating it, so a new block kind on the server appears here with no client change. This also fixes a real annoyance: until now every added block landed at the lattice origin regardless of where the user was looking.

The native menu is suppressed only over the sheet, so the browser's own menu still works over the rails and the dock.

Go: added DisconnectBlock and DELETE /blocks/{id}/connections.

Verified with 15/15 CDP checks, including edge flipping near a viewport corner, arrow-key navigation, Escape and outside-click dismissal without acting, the palette keeping the browser menu, placement within 3px of the click point, and disconnect removing only that block's wires (7 signals -> 4).

Rebuilt the workbench as an annunciator panel: machined dark housing (topbar, rails, dock bezel, readout rail) framing two lit displays (the vellum sheet and the results dock).

Tokens, all derived in :root — sheet #eef1ef, housing #16201e / raised #1f2c29 / deep #0f1817, ink #101a18 + muted #4a5b56, ink-inverse #e8efec + muted #93a8a2, signal #e2673a (wires and output ports only), probe #35b39c with probe-deep #0d6156 for the same affordance on vellum, caution #d9a441, alarm #ef7f6a. Category accents kept but split into a bright pair for the housing and a deep pair for the sheet: source 3fbfa6/10756a, math a189e0/5b40a8, sum d9a441/8a6410, continuous 7aa8de/33629b, sink 93b8ae/3c6058. Gain moved off orange onto violet so orange means signal and nothing else.

Type: Georgia gone entirely. Grotesque for labels, ui-monospace with tabular-nums promoted to a first-class role for every numeric readout (cursor, zoom, grid, counts, gains, block parameter summaries, metrics, timestamps, chart axes, kbd). Scale 11/12/13/15/19/24 with an 11px floor.

Readout rail: the status bar is now a segmented monospace instrument strip — solver lamp + state, live cursor sheet coordinates, zoom, grid pitch, selection count, block count, signal count, then the message slot and key hints. IDs: #readout-rail, #readout-solver-field (data-state idle/running/solved/fault), #readout-solver, #readout-cursor with #readout-cursor-x / #readout-cursor-y, #readout-zoom, #readout-grid, #readout-selection (data-count lights the cell), #readout-blocks, #readout-signals, #interaction-status retained.

Contrast, all AA: 15.6:1 ink on vellum, 6.3:1 muted on vellum, 14.3:1 ink-inverse on housing, 6.6:1 muted on housing (5.8:1 on raised). Two colours had to change to clear AA — the direction pill moved to signal-lit #ef8a5e (4.3:1 -> 5.8:1) and the palette add-glyph to the muted inverse (3.5:1 -> 5.8:1).

Three real defects found and fixed while verifying:
1. The rail's nowrap message was setting the min-content width of the shell's single grid column, so the topbar, studio-grid and rail all rendered 11px wider than the viewport at 1280 and 92px wider at 1099. Fixed with grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) on .workbench plus overflow:hidden on the rail.
2. The number inputs' outline:0 beat the :focus-visible rule, leaving the duration and sample fields with no ring. Rings now sit on the field wrapper, and housing fields get color-scheme:dark so the spinners stop flashing white.
3. Raising chart type above the floor made the fixed 780-unit viewBox render axis labels at 9.0px at 1280 and 10.3px at 620, and pushed the 'seconds' caption on top of the last tick. Fixed by dropping the dock to one column below 1400px, a 640px floor width on the chart with the panel scrolling instead of the page, and nudging the caption into the tick gap.

Verified over CDP in headless Chrome against a rebuilt binary at 1440x900, 1280x720, 1099, 980, 860 and 620: 10/10 scripted checks pass — cursor readout tracks the pointer (0270,0110 -> 0861,0480), rail zoom agrees with the toolbar, the cursor cell width is identical across every digit combination (no jitter), zero rendered text below 11px at any breakpoint, chart labels render 11.5-14px everywhere, selected blocks carry a 2px outline as well as a hue change, and reduced-motion zeroes every transition and both animations. A 26-element keyboard tab walk shows a 2px focus-visible ring on every control, #5fd8c0 on the housing and #0d6156 on the vellum. No horizontal overflow at any width; rails collapse to a category-coloured glyph strip. Server and temp db cleaned up; nothing committed.

Drag-to-wire between ports, with click-then-click retained.

Pressing an output port captures the pointer on the canvas and enters wiring; the target under the cursor is found geometrically with elementFromPoint, so the draft edge keeps tracking after leaving the port. Release over a valid input commits, elsewhere cancels. A press with no travel leaves the sticky click-then-click mode armed, so both gestures coexist and the keyboard path survives.

Feedback: .hover-target enlarges and lights the port under the pointer, .hover-refused shows a not-allowed cursor. A self-connection is refused on the client with a status message instead of a server round trip and an error banner.

Fixed the port-occlusion defect recorded on this task: .block-card is position:absolute with z-index:5, so each card is its own stacking context and a card later in DOM order painted over an earlier card's ports. Cards now rise on hover and focus-within, and higher again while wiring.

Ports also gained an invisible hit pad sized calc(22px / var(--zoom)), so the target stays roughly constant on screen and wiring is still practical at 40%.

Verified with 11/11 CDP checks: wiring by drag at 100% and 27% zoom, clean cancel over empty canvas, self-connection refused without a banner, sticky mode still wiring, and elementFromPoint confirming no port is buried (0/13 at rest, 0 of the on-screen ports at 202%).

Note: the test initially failed because every input in the seeded flowsheet is already wired, so the server correctly rejected each pair. The suite now adds a free block first.

Left alone deliberately: .canvas-legend paints above the sheet. It is a corner overlay chip with pointer-events:none, so it never intercepts a gesture; being on top is correct for chrome.

Documented and verified the workbench.

Added docs/workbench-ergonomics.md recording the interaction model, the HTMX-swap constraint that shapes the whole client, the sheet geometry contract between Go and the browser, the snapping and selection models, every key binding with its rationale, the localStorage keys, the batch endpoints, and a verification record. It also records three traps for anyone writing more browser checks, each of which cost real debugging time here.

Rewrote the README's workbench sections, which still documented click-to-wire as the only gesture and made no mention of the shell, the viewport, or the keyboard. Added gesture and keyboard tables, the client-state note, and the go:embed rebuild warning.

Verified: gofmt, go vet, go test -race all clean; type-floor grep clean; 88 CDP checks across six suites; no horizontal overflow at 1440x900, 1280x720, 1099x800, 860 and 620.

data.title: Add project-style flowsheet management
data.body:
## Goal
- Add persistent projects containing multiple named flowsheets, with user-facing create, rename, switch, save, and reopen workflows.

## Decisions
- A project owns one or more top-level flowsheets.
- Creating a project atomically creates its first flowsheet.
- All model edits continue to autosave to the configured SQLite database.
- The studio package owns naming validation, defaults, timestamps, migration, and transactional lifecycle rules.
- The web package owns URLs, HTMX redirects, presentation, and browser navigation.

## Non-goals
- Hierarchical subflowsheet or subsystem blocks.
- Import/export, collaboration, authentication, flow deletion, and project deletion.

## Constraints
- Existing databases must migrate without losing the seeded or user-edited flow.
- Existing block, wiring, simulation, and workbench behavior must remain compatible.
- Deliver in reviewable commits and finish with a pull request.

data.title: Migrate flows into persistent projects
data.body:
## Goal
- Introduce the persistent Project model and migrate every existing flow into one default project without losing data.

## Context
- Change internal/studio/model.go and internal/studio/store.go.
- projects is the authoritative owner of project identity and name; flows gain project_id.
- New databases seed one project containing the existing Reactor temperature loop.
- Legacy databases may have flows but no projects or project_id column.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Project and project-aware Flow types expose only data needed by callers.
- Opening a legacy database creates one default project and associates all existing flows with it.
- Opening the database repeatedly is idempotent.
- Foreign-key and lookup indexes support project-scoped flow queries.
- Existing snapshots and simulations remain readable.

## Validation Gates
- env GOCACHE=/tmp/go-htmx-project-cache go test ./internal/studio

data.title: Own project and flowsheet lifecycle in Studio
data.body:
## Goal
- Add cohesive Studio operations for browsing projects and creating or renaming flowsheets.

## Context
- Change internal/studio/studio.go and focused tests.
- Compare two call shapes before implementation; select intent-revealing operations that hide transaction order, timestamps, default first-flow creation, and validation.
- Normal names are trimmed, required, and bounded by one studio-owned rule.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A workspace query returns the active project, project choices, sibling flowsheets, and active snapshot in deterministic order.
- CreateProject(name) atomically creates a named project and its first flowsheet.
- CreateFlow(projectID, name) creates and returns the new active workspace.
- RenameFlow(flowID, name) updates the displayed name without invalidating model simulation results.
- Invalid names and unknown IDs return existing actionable validation/not-found contracts.
- Lifecycle operations append useful activity and preserve autosave semantics.

## Validation Gates
- env GOCACHE=/tmp/go-htmx-project-cache go test ./internal/studio

data.title: Add project-aware HTML and HTMX routes
data.body:
## Goal
- Expose project-aware page navigation and flowsheet lifecycle actions over HTML and HTMX.

## Context
- Change internal/web/server.go, internal/web/view.go, and server tests.
- Full-page project/flow URLs are web-owned; Studio operations remain free of URL and HTTP knowledge.
- Preserve existing fragment endpoints used by the workbench.

## Acceptance Criteria
- GET / redirects or renders the deterministic current project and flow.
- GET /projects/{projectID}/flows/{flowID} renders a complete page and rejects mismatched project/flow IDs.
- POST /projects creates a project and redirects to its first flow.
- POST /projects/{projectID}/flows creates a flowsheet and redirects to it.
- PUT /flows/{flowID}/name renames the active flowsheet and returns a coherent HTMX workbench.
- Redirect behavior works for normal and HX requests.
- Existing block and simulation handlers render project navigation consistently.

## Validation Gates
- env GOCACHE=/tmp/go-htmx-project-cache go test ./internal/web

data.title: Build the project and flowsheet navigation UI
data.body:
## Goal
- Make project and flowsheet creation, naming, switching, and reopening obvious in the workbench UI.

## Context
- Change internal/web/templates, internal/web/static/app.css, and only the minimal app.js navigation behavior required.
- Reuse the existing visual system and fixed-shell constraints.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The top bar identifies the active project and flowsheet.
- Users can switch projects and sibling flowsheets using durable full-page URLs.
- Users can create a named project and a named flowsheet without leaving the workbench.

## Goal
- Document persistent project workflows and verify the complete change before publication.

## Context
- Update README.md with naming, autosave, reopen, new project, new flowsheet, and database-path instructions.

- A new user can create, name, switch, save, stop, restart, and reopen multiple flowsheets from the README.
